features.name: Plugin delay compensation
features.description: Align every path to the master when plugins report latency.
features.fl_reference: FL Studio compensates plugin latency automatically (mixer), shows it under Audio settings › Device status (input, output and plugin latency) and trims it from renders ('Trim PDC silence', on by default).
features.limeshot_behavior: Automatic, always on. For each mixer track the engine works out the latest arrival of its inputs (plugin channels with their latency; routed tracks through their insert latencies) and delays everything that arrives earlier: the track's sampler/LimeSynth voices, plugin channels with less latency, and routes from tracks with less (one delay line per source track, a tap per route). Latencies come from the plugins (`IAudioProcessor::getLatencySamples`, read again when a plugin reports kLatencyChanged) and are rechecked every 16 blocks; the plan keeps its delay lines across edits, so changing the project does not interrupt the delayed audio. Up to 16 384 frames (about 340 ms at 48 kHz) per path and 64 delay lines; paths beyond that stay uncompensated. Exports leave out the delay (FL's Trim PDC silence). The Audio settings show the total ('Plugin delay compensation: N samples').
acceptance_criteria: Behaves as described under 'LimeShot intended behaviour'.
Has an automated test or a documented manual test procedure.
features.notes: Session 15. Engine test with impulse plugins at block sizes 64, 333 and 1024 (fails without compensation: impulses at 24 000, 24 300 and 25 000). Not checked by ear with a commercial latent plugin (Elephant reports 1080 samples) in the live app. FL's per-track manual PDC and the Trim PDC silence switch are not offered (always on).

features.limeshot_behavior: Each plugin channel and plugin insert has one plugin window, its own OS window titled like FL's ("Vital (Bass)", "OTT (Lead)"), floating above the main window and hidden while another application is active. A click on a plugin channel's button (FL) or a plugin insert's name in the insert chain opens it and a second click closes it; the Editor button in Channel Settings and the insert card opens it too, and the channel menu's Channel Settings opens it on the Settings tab. A tab row at the top: Plugin shows the plugin's own editor (VST3 IPlugView, attached below the tabs on macOS); Settings shows LimeShot's Channel Settings for the channel (name, mixer target, root key, plugin info, parameter list) or the insert's card. On the Plugin tab the window is the editor's size plus the tab row and follows the editor when the plugin resizes itself (IPlugFrame::resizeView); the Settings tab is resizable. The window reopens where it was and on the tab it was on; each window's position, tab, Settings size, keyboard toggle and whether it is open are saved in the .lime with its plugin (not an edit, like the plugin state), and windows that were open reopen with the project (FL does both). A plugin without an editor (or where the platform cannot show one: Windows and Linux so far, headless backends) gets the parameter list on the Plugin tab.
